name: יִשָּׂשכָר
gloss: there is hire; or he bears a wage
summary: Jacob’s ninth son, Leah’s fifth, father of the tribe that camped and marched with Judah and Zebulun (Num 2:5; 10:15); and a Levite gatekeeper, a son of Obed-edom (1Ch 26:5). Leah named him for שָׂכָר twice over: she had “surely hired” Jacob with her son’s mandrakes, and when the boy was born she said “God has given me my שָׂכָר” (Gen 30:16–18). The text writes the name with a second ש that is not read; its first part is read either as יֵשׁ, “there is (hire)”, or as יִשָּׂא, “he carries (a wage)”: the explanation in Genesis rests on שָׂכָר, and the form of the first part is not certain.

evidence.note: Leah to Jacob: שָׂכֹר שְׂכַרְתִּיךָ בְּדוּדָאֵי בְּנִי, “I have surely hired you with my son’s mandrakes.”
“God has given me my שָׂכָר, because I gave my maid to my husband”; and she called his name יִשָּׂשכָר.
Over the host of the tribe of the sons of יִשָּׂשכָר, Nethanel son of Zuar, as the camp set out from Sinai.
Jacob’s blessing: Issachar a strong donkey, who “bowed his shoulder to bear and became a servant at forced labour”: a worker for another, as his name is wage.
The Levite: Obed-edom’s seventh son יִשָׂשכָר, after שָׂכָר Sachar the fourth (1Ch 26:4) and before פְּעֻלְּתַי Peullethai, “my wage”, “for God blessed him”.
Of the tribe of Ἰσαχάρ, twelve thousand sealed.

note: TIPNR names two people, Jacob’s son (with the tribe) and Obed-edom’s son; both are tagged. The written form has ששכר with the second ש unpointed (read יִשָּׂכָר); BDB’s cross-reference key u.bk.af (יִשָּׂשׂכָר) has no tokens and is not named. The database’s entry_root offers נשׂא (“lift”) beside שׂכר for this name; that is the יִשָּׂא reading. 43 tokens under j.dr.ad.
